base_source: TTM after-tax realized income per share: FY2025 $4.76 - H1 2025 $2.12 (Q1 $1.09 + Q2 $1.03) + H1 2026 $2.53 (Q1 $1.24 + Q2 $1.29) = $5.17. Engine OCF base rejected for an alternative manager: consolidated-fund OCF gives latest-FY OE/share $8.91 and a 3-yr median of -$0.76/share (preliminary Tier F artifact). See analysis.md.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.4x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits banks/insurers poorly; grade confidence low
moat_justification: Scale and origination in private credit, $671B AUM / $410B fee-paying AUM, long-dated/perpetual capital, $79B of not-yet-fee-paying AUM and diversified Credit/Real Assets/PE/Secondaries distribution — against no structural pricing power (LPs reallocate each vintage among Blackstone/Apollo/KKR/Brookfield/Blue Owl, direct-lending spreads compressing), earnings geared to the private-credit cycle, growth partly bought (GCP International, $3.91B, closed Mar 2025), and private-credit/insurance regulatory overhang.
name: Ares Management Corporation
one_liner: Scaled private-credit-led alt manager, moat 6/10 — the engine's Tier F is a consolidated-fund OCF artifact (median OE -$0.76/sh rejected); on TTM after-tax realized earnings of $5.17/share the $118.15 price (22.9x) yields an 11.9% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $84.17, and it clears 15% only at ~$84 (~$67 with a margin of safety).
